title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover hysteresis
author: Priya Narang
release_notes: Hotfix: prevent failover storms by adding hysteresis and ordering guarantees to SLO enforcer backoff; no API changes.
description: Context: After last week's regional outage, the SLO enforcer could trigger near-simultaneous regional failovers during backoff transitions which resulted in cascading capacity pressure (see SUP-675). This PR implements a targeted hotfix to add hysteresis and ordering guarantees to the enforcer's backoff/failover path so regional failovers are staggered and the system can recover more gracefully. Motivation: reduce cascading failovers and noisy backoff oscillation without changing customer-facing SLO config. Changes are conservative and feature-flagged for immediate rollback if needed. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failure pattern in synthetic chaos tests - [x] Add hysteresis and ordering guard in enforcer - [x] Ensure backoff timers respect per-region jitter windows - [x] Add metrics/traces for decision points and TTLs - [x] Integration tests + canary rollout plan - [x] Docs/console note for operators (short) Design summary: 1) Hysteresis window: when a region is marked for backoff, it now enters a hysteresis window (default 30s) during which additional failover decisions are suppressed for that region. 2) Regional ordering token: a lightweight token store (in-memory leader-election with fallback to distributed lease) ensures that at most N regions per account can initiate failover within a rolling window. This prevents global storms when many regions are degraded. 3) Jittered backoff: backoff timers are jittered based on region load to avoid synchronized retries. 4) Observability: new counters and traces at the decision point (enforcer.decision, enforcer.hysteresis_suppressed, enforcer.token_acquired) and a dashboard tile added to Console. Rollout plan: - Feature-flag off by default on main - Canary: enable for internal orgs in us-west-2 only for 15 minutes, monitor enforcer metrics and infra cost - Gradual rollout to other regions over 2 hours if canary stable - Immediate rollback via flag if suppression metrics spike or failover latencies exceed thresholds Tests: unit tests for hysteresis/timer logic, integration tests simulating multi-region degradation and confirming at-most-N regional failover ordering, synthetic chaos deck reproduced the original outage pattern (attached). Backwards compatibility: no changes to public API or customer SLO semantics. Ops notes: requires config map key slo_enforcer.hysteresis_window with sensible default; if disabled we revert to previous behavior. Related: ENG-1124 (slo enforcer stability), ENG-1130 (regional failover incident follow-up).

review_comments: Ethan Miller: Can we avoid a full distributed lease for the token store? Priya: we keep an in-memory leader with a simple fallback to the existing distributed lease - added tests to validate both paths.
Ana Gomez: Is hysteresis_window configurable per-customer? Priya: exposed as cluster config; we intentionally keep a sane global default and will evaluate per-customer tuning in a follow-up.
Liam O'Connor: Please add an integration that asserts at-most-N regions failover within 1m window. Priya: added integration test and chaos deck reproducing the issue.
Infra CI: observed flakiness in 1 e2e case, reran and passed - noted in CI checks.
